why.text: Hot summers and cold winters on potassium-rich red soils give fresh, aromatic wines. Whites from Malvar and Torrontés stand out.

styles.text: Light, fresh whites and rosados (Torrontés), plus moderately tannic reds: young, aged or carbonic-maceration.

climate.text: From 40 °C in summer to -8 °C in winter, with about 500 mm of rain a year.

soil.text: Deep red silty-clay soil with gravel; alkaline, low in organic matter and phosphorus, rich in potassium.

tastes.text: Whites: yellow, light, perfumed and pleasantly acidic; Torrontés intensely aromatic. Rosés: pink, red fruit and flowers, fresh. Reds: cherry, garnet or ruby, fruity, moderately tannic; aged ones tile-coloured, toasty, spiced.

styles.name: Maceración carbónica
styles.text: Silky, very tannic, with a persistent fruity finish.

styles.name: Fermentado en barrica
styles.text: White or rosé; fruit and floral aromas balanced with barrel.

styles.name: Crianza, Reserva y Gran Reserva
styles.text: Tile tones; oak and stewed fruit, toast, spice; fleshy, persistent.

why.text: Low yields (about 3,000 kg/ha) give deeply coloured reds with ripe fruit. The sierra zones add minerality, while the chalky south-east adds ripeness.

styles.text: Fruity whites, rosados from dry to sweet, warm tannic reds, and quality sparkling wines.

soil.text: Chalky ground in the south-east; the sierra zones give mineral, scrubland notes.

tastes.text: Whites: pale straw, fruity; gold when aged. Rosés: strawberry, raspberry or salmon pink; red fruit, fresh. Reds: violet to cherry, ruby to tile when aged; fruity, tannic, warm, persistent; oak, spice and dried fruit with age.

styles.name: Vino espumoso de calidad
styles.text: Fine, abundant, lasting bubbles; fruity aromas; fresh and sharp.

styles.name: Crianza y Reserva
styles.text: White wines age to deep golden or old gold.

why.text: Highly alkaline soil and a cool area make the grapes ripen slowly and evenly.

styles.text: Red wines only, deep in colour and rich in polyphenols.

climate.text: A cool area, where the grapes ripen slowly and evenly.

soil.text: Highly limestone and strongly alkaline.

altitude.text: Vines grow at 845 to 1,005 m, sometimes on steep slopes and terraces.

tastes.text: Cherry red, bright or dark, medium to medium-high depth. Floral nose, with wild-berry fruit or jam. Polished, creamy tannins, sometimes firm; well balanced.

why.text: An extreme continental climate meets sandy, acidic soil poor in lime. The wines are warm and full-bodied, with high alcohol.

styles.text: Dry to sweet whites and rosados, young and oak-aged reds, and sparkling wines.

climate.text: Extreme continental: long cold winters, hot summers and very little rain.

soil.text: Sandy, acidic soil with very little lime.

tastes.text: Whites: pale straw, fruity with floral touches; oak versions pastry and toast. Rosés: strawberry pink, fresh. Reds: cherry to dark garnet; blackberry, redcurrant, flowers; fleshy, warm, well-integrated tannins; long, intense finish.

styles.name: Roble
styles.text: White with pastry notes such as cream and a toasty base.

styles.name: Crianza, Reserva y Gran Reserva
styles.text: Cherry to ruby-tile; structured, oak notes, long and intense.

styles.name: Vino espumoso
styles.text: Fine, lasting bubbles; fruity aromas; reservas more intense.

why.text: Altitude and potassium-rich soils, with low-density bush vines, give balanced grapes. The wines are acidic and made to last in bottle.

styles.text: Reds, young whites and barrel-fermented or aged whites, rosados, and quality sparkling wines.

soil.text: Fine-textured, deep, tending to chalky; clay-loam to sandy-loam; rich in potassium.

altitude.text: 500 to 800 m in the west half; 600 to 1,200 m in the east.

tastes.text: Reds: deep colour, intense fruity and floral aromas; powerful, full-bodied, harmonious. Whites: pale yellow, fruity and fresh; barrel-fermented straw to golden, toasty. Rosés: strawberry or raspberry pink, fruity.

styles.name: Blanco fermentado en barrica
styles.text: Straw to golden; toasty barrel notes, soft texture, fruity finish.

styles.name: Espumoso de calidad
styles.text: Pale, small persistent bubbles; fruity aroma; fresh and balanced.

why.text: Clay topsoil gives the wines power and intensity, and the limestone below gives their tannins elegance and a velvety texture.

styles.text: Red wines only, deep in colour, made at the estate's own winery.

climate.text: Continental, with dry hot summers and cold winters. Mean 17 °C in winter, 26 °C in summer; 450 mm of rain a year.

soil.text: Clay topsoil 30 to 50 cm deep over fragmented limestone; basic (pH above 8) and well drained.

tastes.text: Very deep colour. Nose: spice and tobacco, with balsamic and cocoa notes. Palate: powerful and fleshy, with fruit and soft tannins; persistent.

why.text: Very salty soils high in potassium and low air humidity keep the grapes small, with more skin to pulp.

styles.text: Mostly red blends of the estate's grapes, plus a wine from the year's best grape. A barrel-aged white too.

climate.text: Low relative humidity, averaging 15% over the whole growing season.

soil.text: Alkaline limestone soil that is very salty and very poor in nutrients; high in potassium.

tastes.text: Reds: medium-high depth, bright, dense; red and black fruit; fresh, full, long finish. White: bright; fruit, tropical notes, toast, nuts; round, with butter and light smoke.

why.text: Between two river valleys, summers are hot and sunny with almost no rain. On calcareous clay soils, Bobal gives aromatic, deeply coloured wines.

styles.text: Dry to sweet whites and rosados; young, oak-aged and carbonic-maceration reds; sparkling white and rosé.

climate.text: High temperatures, almost no rain from May to September, and many hours of sun.

soil.text: Clay soils with a limestone base, from the sediments of two rivers.

tastes.text: Whites: very pale yellow with green glints, fruity. Rosés: strawberry, raspberry, bright, fresh, harmonious. Reds: cherry to ruby with violet; wild red fruit, long. Aged reds: garnet to tile; vanilla, toast, spice, jam.

styles.name: Fermentado en barrica
styles.text: Primary fruit and floral aromas in balance with the barrel.

styles.name: Crianza, Reserva y Gran Reserva
styles.text: Garnet or ruby with tile tones; vanilla, toast; medium-high to high tannin.

styles.name: Vino espumoso
styles.text: White or rosé; small persistent bubbles; fruity, fresh and balanced.

why.text: North-facing vines in a hill's early-afternoon shade, on acid siliceous soil, give wines of almost Atlantic character, without warm notes.

styles.text: Dry reds, varietal or blended; the blends age 3 to 24 months. One dry Chardonnay white with oak notes.

climate.text: Wetter than neighbouring regions, with several microclimates. Cold air pools in hollows, where fog lingers.

soil.text: Siliceous and acid.

tastes.text: Reds: ruby to cherry red. Berries and spice with tobacco and scrub; dry and long, with present tannin. White: greenish straw. Tropical and white stone fruit with butter; dry and almost oily, with a fresh finish.

styles.name: Tinto Cabernet Sauvignon
styles.text: Ruby red. Pepper and tobacco, with cedar and scrub from ageing; dry and polished.

styles.name: Tinto Syrah
styles.text: Cherry red (picota). Berries and leather; dry and fruity, filling the mouth.

styles.name: Tinto Petit Verdot
styles.text: Dark cherry red (picota). Red fruit with spice and scrub; tannic, well structured.

styles.name: Blanco Chardonnay
styles.text: Greenish straw. Exotic fruit and butter with lees; dry, almost oily, fresh finish.

why.text: The Júcar canyon brings more rain than the surrounding flatland. Lake-deposit soils give soft, balanced wines with good acidity.

styles.text: Dry and sweet whites and rosados; young, traditional, crianza and reserva reds.

climate.text: The Júcar canyon causes more rain than the surrounding area. The document gives no figures.

soil.text: Lake deposits: silty sands, salty clays, gravel and rounded dolomitic limestone cemented by clay.

tastes.text: Whites: pale yellow, fruity, soft. Rosés: pink, moderate body. Young reds: cherry-red, red fruit, powerful, round. Aged reds: ruby to tile; floral, spice, balsamic, toast; velvety, long; vanilla, pepper and cocoa after wood.

styles.name: Tradición
styles.text: Red and purple tones; intense, frank aromas; long, intense finish.

styles.name: Crianza y Reserva
styles.text: Ruby to cherry with tile tones; ripe red fruit; potent after wood.

why.text: Dry, chalky plains get 3,000 hours of sun and 300 to 350 mm of rain. Wines are colourful and aromatic, balanced by low yields.

styles.text: Whites and rosados, young or traditional; oak and aged reds; naturally sweet wine; semi-sparkling and sparkling wines.

climate.text: Extreme continental: high temperatures, 300 to 350 mm of rain a year and about 3,000 hours of sun.

soil.text: Miocene limestone, marl and sand, brown to red-brown; chalky soils give full-bodied reds.

tastes.text: Whites: yellow short of gold, fruity, slightly acidic; oaked ones toasty with vanilla. Rosés: pale pink to red, fruity. Reds: violet to garnet, fruity, tannic; oaked ones vanilla; aged ones tile-edged, soft.

styles.name: Tradicional Naturalmente Dulce
styles.text: White; glyceric, raisins and stone fruit, velvety, long finish.

styles.name: Roble
styles.text: Red garnet to ruby; vanilla; persistent and balanced.

styles.name: Crianza, Reserva y Gran Reserva
styles.text: White or red; vanilla and toast; reds from cherry to tile.

styles.name: Vino de aguja
styles.text: White, rosé or red; fruity, broad and balanced, carbonic gas noticeable.

why.text: South-facing slopes beside natural lagoons give very ripe fruit aromas with a fresh feel in the mouth.

styles.text: Red wine made at least 90% from Tempranillo.

climate.text: A sunny, south-facing site sheltered from north winds. Tempranillo ripens early here; harvest starts 15 days before nearby vineyards.

tastes.text: Very dark red with violet rims. Nose: very ripe fruit with roasted notes and a mineral touch. Palate: powerful and full; fruit with vanilla and soft cinnamon; fleshy and long.

why.text: Lithium-rich soil gives wines with up to ten times the lithium of nearby wines.

styles.text: Red and white wines, marked by a high lithium content from the soil.

soil.text: Sandy loam with volcanic basalt and a basic pH; lithium at 0.86 to 2.9 mg/kg.

tastes.text: Reds: cherry or deep red, strong nose, tasty, fleshy, powerful. White: clear, pale straw with golden rims; white fruit, fresh, balanced acidity, long finish.

why.text: Almansa is a high plateau with an extreme continental climate and limestone-rich soil. Yields of 4,500 kg/ha concentrate colour and tannin in the wines.

styles.text: Young and barrel-aged whites, rosados and reds, dry to sweet; reds also crianza, reserva and gran reserva.

climate.text: Extreme continental: very cold dry winters, very hot summers, under 250 mm of rain a year on average, mostly spring and late summer.

soil.text: Rich in limestone, from thin stony patches to deeper sandy ones.

altitude.text: Plateau from 400 m at Fuente la Higuera to 700 m at Almansa.

tastes.text: Whites: light, sustained yellow, mildly aromatic. Rosés: strawberry to raspberry pink, fruity. Reds: violet, deep colour, fleshy, lightly tannic; oaked ones toasty. Aged reds: cherry or garnet, tile tones, fruit and spice.

styles.name: Roble
styles.text: Red; medium persistence with toasty touches.

styles.name: Fermentado en barrica
styles.text: White; straw to gold; primary and toasty aromas; soft, with fruity finish.

styles.name: Crianza, Reserva y Gran Reserva
styles.text: Red; fruit and oak well joined, or spice; medium tannin.

why.text: The grapes develop slowly here, which gives polished, deep-coloured wines with a high concentration of substances.

styles.text: Golden whites with yellow fruit and citrus notes; blended reds with deep colour.

climate.text: Dry and continental. Very cold winters, with many days below 0 °C and several snowfalls. Very windy.

soil.text: Sandy loam with pebbles; low fertility.

tastes.text: White: golden yellow. Yellow fruit such as banana and mango, with grapefruit; fruity palate. Red: deep colour; ripe red fruit. Silky and persistent, with a long, slightly bitter finish.

why.text: At 1,080 m, in dry continental air with big day-night swings, the wines keep good acidity and suit ageing.

styles.text: Whites from Chardonnay, including a late harvest. Reds, young or aged up to Gran Reserva.

climate.text: Continental, with very dry air and a big difference between day and night while the grapes ripen.

soil.text: Poor, stony clay-limestone soils. They drain well and are basic, with pH around 8.

tastes.text: Chardonnay: yellow to gold; fruity and floral nose. Young reds: very deep violet and red; long, round finish. Aged reds: deep colour, turning garnet and tile with longer ageing; fruit and oak.

styles.name: Partly barrel-fermented Chardonnay
styles.text: Fruity and floral aromas with oak; long finish.

styles.name: Vendimia Tardía
styles.text: Late-harvest Chardonnay. Fruity and sweet notes on the nose; acidity and sugar in balance.

styles.name: Barrica, crianza, reserva
styles.text: Aged reds keep deep colour; longer ageing brings garnet and tile tones.

styles.name: Gran Reserva
styles.text: Red and tile tones. Ripe fruit and clear ageing aromas; oak tannins, not harsh.

why.text: A Mediterranean climate with low rain in key months cuts disease. Reds are rich in tannin and colour, while whites are fruity with medium-high acidity.

styles.text: Fruity whites, rosados and reds rich in tannin and colour; whites and reds also aged (crianza, reserva).

climate.text: Mediterranean, with low rainfall in the decisive months of the growing season, so little fungal disease.

tastes.text: Whites: greenish to straw, white, yellow, citrus or exotic fruit. Rosés: pink to red; red or black fruit. Reds: violet tones, medium colour; red, black or raisined fruit. Aged wines: wood and toast.

styles.name: Crianza, Reserva y Gran Reserva
styles.text: Wood and toast aromas and flavours; whites soft to golden yellow.

why.text: Dark volcanic-zone soils warm up early. Dry air and about 400 mm of rain let vines ripen with little disease.

styles.text: Dry to sweet whites, rosados and reds, from young to gran reserva; sparkling white and rosé; some over-ripe red.

climate.text: Mean 15.6 °C, no more than about 400 mm of rain, 52% humidity, over 2,800 sun hours; disease risk almost nil.

soil.text: Dark clay-loam soils, often stony; low in calcium, high in potassium; volcanic rock.

altitude.text: Gentle hills at 700 to 900 m, small plains at 630 to 650 m.

tastes.text: Whites: yellow range; white and tropical fruit, white flowers, citrus. Rosés: violet-pink to salmon; red and black fruit. Reds: red range without orange; red and black fruit, spice, toasty oak; medium acidity and tannin.

styles.name: Clásico
styles.text: Bright; medium or high colour; floral, fruity, spiced aromas.

styles.name: Roble
styles.text: Red fruit, spice and at least one of nut, toast, balsamic, mineral.

styles.name: Crianza, Reserva y Gran Reserva
styles.text: Reds reach ochre or brown; stewed fruit, nuts, toast, balsamic.

why.text: A dry continental climate and chalky, humus-poor soil stress the vines. Low yields give well-structured, complex reds.

styles.text: Whites, rosados, reds including a traditional style, and sparkling wine.

climate.text: Dry continental; high summer temperatures ease off late, slowing the end of ripening and keeping aromas.

soil.text: Chalky, poor in organic matter, pH 7.5 to 8.5, easy for roots to penetrate; reflects sunlight, stores heat.

tastes.text: Whites: pale yellow, golden after barrel; fine, clean, discreetly fruity. Rosés: pink with red and violet; fresh, fruity. Reds: picota to violet cherry or ruby; subtle aroma growing with time; soft, warm, long finish.

styles.name: Tinto Tradicional
styles.text: Violet to garnet red; frank, fruity, medium aromatic intensity.

styles.name: Vino espumoso
styles.text: Pale or golden; fine, persistent bubbles; clean, fruity aromas.

why.text: Lime-rich soils high in calcium and a mild river-and-reservoir climate give fine, balanced wines with a scrub note.

styles.text: Dry and semi-sweet whites, some from red grapes. Rosado from Petit Verdot. Red blends, and a sweet Merlot red.

climate.text: Milder than the surrounding area: the river and the nearby reservoir limit extreme weather.

soil.text: Limestone soil of light texture, shallow and well drained; medium fertility; calcium above 15 meq/100 g (over 3,000 ppm).

tastes.text: Whites: lemon to gold; citrus and tropical fruit. Rosé: bright raspberry pink; cherry or strawberry candy. Reds: cherry red; red fruit and balsamic notes. Sweet red: figs and jam.

styles.name: Blanco parcialmente fermentado en barrica
styles.text: Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc; 15% or more of the must ferments in oak.

styles.name: Blanco de uvas tintas
styles.text: White made from red grapes; fermented in steel tanks at 11 to 20 °C.

styles.name: Tinto coupage autóctonas con foráneas
styles.text: Blend of native and foreign red grapes; at least 30% spends 3+ months in oak.

styles.name: Vino dulce
styles.text: Sweet Merlot red, grapes over 280 g/l sugar; stopped at 46 to 90 g/l.

why.text: High-strontium soils in a sediment-filled river hollow give intense wines with a marked mineral note.

styles.text: Oak-aged reds (blends, or single-grape Merlot) and a single-grape Sauvignon Blanc white.

climate.text: Temperate Mediterranean with continental traits: 14 to 16 °C mean, 450 mm rain a year. Woods shield the vines from the hot, dry Levante wind.

soil.text: Red Mediterranean alfisols over limestone, sandy loam to clay. Coarse river pebbles abound. Strontium is high.

altitude.text: Flat ground at 700 m above sea level.

tastes.text: Reds: ripe cherry (picota) red; red and black fruit with a mineral note; broad and fleshy. Whites: straw yellow; white stone fruit and floral notes; fresh and silky.

styles.name: Tinto de ensamblaje
styles.text: Red blend; at least 3 months in oak and 1 month in bottle.

styles.name: Tinto monovarietal Merlot
styles.text: Single-grape Merlot red; 6 months in oak and 6 in bottle at least.

styles.name: Blanco monovarietal Sauvignon Blanc
styles.text: Single-grape white, fermented in steel tank at 10 to 21 °C.

why.text: Hills around the riverside vineyard make it a cool site, raising acidity and phenolic compounds in the grapes.

styles.text: Oak-aged reds only, single-grape or blended; minimum barrel time runs from 30 days to 24 months.

climate.text: Continental Mediterranean: hot summers, cold winters. Usually over 2,500 sun hours a year. Late spring frosts. Rain well above the rest of La Mancha.

soil.text: Mostly limestone. The main rock is marl, an unconsolidated mix of clay and limestone. Loam texture, pH about 8.

altitude.text: Vineyard at 695 m beside the Peñarroya reservoir, ringed by hills.

tastes.text: Six-month wines: purple or picota red, violet rims; fruit with floral scents; soft and fresh. Longer-aged wines: cherry red, garnet-tile rims; ripe fruit, liquorice, balsam; fleshy, with creamy oak notes.

styles.name: Colección Privada
styles.text: Tempranillo and Cabernet Sauvignon blend; at least 13 months in oak.

styles.name: Cabernet Sauvignon de Familia
styles.text: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon; at least 24 months in barrel, then 18 in bottle.

styles.name: Petit Verdot 12 meses
styles.text: 100% Petit Verdot; at least 12 months in oak.

styles.name: Tempranillo y Cabernet Sauvignon
styles.text: Blend of the two grapes; at least 6 months in oak.

why.text: Poor, acid soils low in potassium and calcium give reds fresh acidity and a lasting ruby colour, even at a southern latitude.

styles.text: Dry reds only, with barrel notes; fresh and young in character.

climate.text: Atlantic influence and a nearby reservoir temper winter and summer. Big day-night swings. 650 mm of rain, mostly autumn and spring; almost dry summers.

soil.text: Very old red soil, acid (pH below 6) and rich in iron. Half the topsoil is stone, including quartzite.

altitude.text: Vineyards at 650 m, at the foot of a sierra that reaches 1,279 m.

tastes.text: Deep ruby red. Intense red fruit, plus spice and toast from the barrels. Good structure and persistence; balanced acidity; fresh and young.

why.text: The high plateau (940 to 1,000 m) gives cooler days and a slow, balanced ripening that keeps the acidity.

styles.text: Reds aged 11+ months, then 6+ in bottle. White Gewürztraminer aged 3+ months on its lees.

climate.text: Continental Mediterranean; day-night swings over 20 °C at ripening. Wind and cold-air drainage protect against frost. Late-August storms cool the ripening days.

soil.text: Acid soils, low in calcium and organic matter. Fairly high in clay. Regular liming partly offsets the acidity.

tastes.text: Whites: straw yellow; citrus, floral, tropical fruit, apple; light acidity, bitter finish. Reds: picota red; fresh red fruit, floral, spice, smoke; light acidity, bitter finish.

styles.name: Vino tinto
styles.text: Red aged 11 months or more (5+ in oak), then 6+ in bottle.

styles.name: Vino blanco Gewürztraminer
styles.text: White aged 3+ months on lees in steel or oak, then 1+ in bottle.

why.text: Big day-night swings and more rain than the rest of the region give grapes a strong tannic structure for barrel and bottle ageing.

styles.text: Whites and reds. Both have toasty notes; in the red they come from wood.

climate.text: The Bullaque river and the sierra's shelter from north winds moderate extremes. Big day-night swings; more rain than the rest of the region.

soil.text: Acid raña soil, low in calcium and rich in silica. Iron and aluminium are also high.

tastes.text: White: intense yellow; stone and tropical fruit on a herbal background. Fresh and round, with a toasty, slightly bitter finish. Red: intense red with garnet rims; red fruit and scrub with toasted wood. Round, with slightly firm tannin.
